need.query: Find and compare options for searching a compact public collection in a browser and a machine client.

claims.text: String.prototype.includes reports whether a string contains the supplied substring. It does not supply fuzzy or semantic search.
MiniSearch supports in-memory full-text search in Node and browsers, including prefix matching, fuzzy matching and field boosting.
Pagefind derives a search index from generated HTML and can restrict matches using named filter metadata.

candidates.name: Shared literal text filter
candidates.reason: Use one small filter for the same public IDs and exact constraints in browser and CLI. Each entered term must appear in the indexed fields.
limitations: Typos, synonyms and whole natural-language questions can omit useful options.
The local matched-task checks establish behavior on this small collection, not general research superiority.

candidates.name: MiniSearch for fuzzy and ranked text
candidates.reason: Revisit if typo tolerance, prefix completion or ranked lexical results change human task outcomes. Share the same configuration across Node and browser.
limitations: No library was installed or exercised. No comparative performance or relevance benefit is established here.
Fuzzy lexical matches still do not interpret an open-world research need.

candidates.name: Pagefind for a generated document site
candidates.reason: Revisit when the public collection becomes a multi-page document site with substantial prose. Its HTML index fits that responsibility better than this structured record view.
limitations: No Pagefind index was built. API/browser identity and filtering parity would need a discriminating integration trial.
This comparison uses primary documentation plus a bounded local implementation trial. Selection does not install software or grant execution authority.
